answer: The sparrow report shows the merge explicitly at each zenith. Each collapsed cluster gets one plume weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 268 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 270 times the capital for one share. A farm of 2306 identities would post 2446 proofs and burn roughly 85 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
